description.narrative: Productivity South Africa (SA), and the Productivity Training Institute (PTI) of the National Bargaining Council for the Clothing Manufacturing Industry (NBCCMI) adopted in June 2020 and operationalized the ILO Sustaining Competitive and Responsible Enterprises (SCORE) programme between October 2019 to June 2021 to promote productivity improvements in 17 export clothing manufacturing firms in key manufacturing clusters across the provinces of Kwazulu Natal, Western Cape and Gauteng. A national decision to implement SCORE in the clothing manufacturing sector was taken by the Government of South Africa and the Social Partners at the November 2018 Presidential Jobs Summit. After a period of planning during the first half of 2019, the first training of trainers took place in October 2019. The Corona virus pandemic delayed the implementation of SCORE, but the programme was finally completed in June 2021 with six national trainers being certified, two of whom are from Productivity SA. The NBCCMI has subsequently mobilized an additional R280'000 from the Fibre Processing and Manufacturing Sector Education Training Authority (FP&M SETA) to continue the SCORE rollout and there is strong national interest in rolling out SCORE to additional key economic manufacturing sectors. At a national knowledge sharing webinar on SCORE held in April 2021, the national stakeholders, including NBCCMI and Productivity SA, agreed to continue with the SCORE rollout across the country. There was equally a strong buy-in for the South African Clothing and Textile Workers Union (SACTWU), the biggest trade union in the sector. The SCORE rigorous monitoring and evaluation system with Enterprise Visit Reports (EVRs) and the Final Progress Assessment (FPA) by each trainer and vetted by the international expert trainers showed that the programme reached more than 2,000 workers in clothing manufacturing firms of which 78% were women workers. (see comments section on Productivity SA) The ILO engaged with the National Bargaining Council for the Clothing Manufacturing Industry (NBCCMI) on the SCORE programme. Following the NBCCMI agreement to roll out SCORE in April 2020, the ILO and NBCCMI were able to implement the SCORE programme with 2.1 million Rands funded by the European Delegation Capacity Building Programme for Employment Promotion (CBPEP) in South Africa. The ILO then supported NBCCMI, CBPEP and Productivity South Africa to design the rollout programme and implementation plan across three targeted provinces, notably KwaZulu Natal, Western Cape and Gauteng. ILO assisted in the recruitment of two international SCORE Expert Trainers to participate in the selection of national trainers and supported NBCCMI and CBPEP in the identification, screening and selection of national trainers. ILO with the support of the SCORE Expert Trainers then facilitated the first SCORE Training of Trainers for 10 trainers of which 50% were women. Lastly, the ILO provided technical support to the full implementation of SCORE in the participating firms and to the certification process of national trainers by reviewing trainers' training.

description.narrative:
The National Department of Trade, Industry and Competition integrated the Social and Solidarity Economy policy as a Key Performance Indicator in the 2021/2022 Annual Performance Plan of the Department that was adopted and published in March 2021. Part of the operationalization of the Annual Performance Plan is to facilitate a process towards the development and adoption of a White Paper on the Social and Solidarity Economy. The draft policy has passed important approval milestones, including approval by the Economic Sectors, Investment, Employment and Infrastructure Development Cluster in December 2020; provisional Social and Economic Impact Assessment approval by the Presidency in December 2020; and the Technical Ministers and Members of the Executive Council in March 2021. The draft policy has now been submitted to the Ministry of Trade and Industry and Competition before final submission for Cabinet approval. In the previous biennium, the ILO with support from the Government of Flanders, coordinated the start of national consultations towards the development of a Social and Solidarity Economy Policy. Building on these consultations, the ILO facilitated further engagement in the current biennium towards organizing consultation webinars on the green paper, and building on research undertaken to inform the writing of the draft policy. The ILO also contributed inputs in the development of a web-platform on the social economy that will be published as a repository of information on consultations undertaken on the green paper. The ILO also commissioned a number of reports to support the transition of the Green Paper to a White Paper, including a report on the process followed in developing the Green Paper, a research study identifying the characteristics of the social economy and an analysis of the policies alignment with national and international frameworks such as the Decent Work Country Programme, Abidjan Declaration and Sustainable Development Goals. In collaboration with the ITC-ILO, a localised training programme for the social and solidarity economy is being developed, to address skills gaps identified as a priority during the national consultation processes.
The ILO regularly shared updates on the policy formulation with the Decent Work Steering Committee of the National Economic Development Advisory Council (NEDLAC) to elicit inputs by the tripartite-plus constituents). ILO support was also directed towards establishing an Expert Reference Panel convened September - December 2020.
